assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED opened a new regime of light-matter interaction on a chip (strong coupling of a superconducting artificial atom to a single microwave photon), and became the architecture for dispersive readout, gates and entanglement in superconducting processors. It is a clean demonstration of fundamental quantum physics made controllable, and it has been reproduced and extended across many laboratories. It follows naturally from the recognition of macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf (2004) set out the theory and first strong-coupling experiment; Wallraff and Schoelkopf led the experimental groups, with Blais as the key theorist. Girvin and Devoret are not in the supplied credit, so the trio is a fair but not unique configuration, and the overlap with the 2025 laureates complicates how much credit remains.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: two decades of independent confirmation, stable interpretation, and wide adoption. Timely, being the natural next step after the 2025 prize.
uncertainties: The omission of Girvin and Devoret from the supplied credit may be contested.
Overlap with the 2025 prize may be judged too close to recent recognition.
I work in this area and defer to colleagues on conflict of interest and on how the credit should be split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised Hubbard-model physics with exquisite control: the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, fermionic Hubbard physics, and single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy. It created the field of analogue quantum simulation and has been reproduced widely.
assessment.attribution: Theoretical proposals (Jaksch, Zoller, Cirac and others) and the experiments (Greiner, Bloch, Esslinger) are separable; the credited list has five names, so a prize must choose between theory and experiment. I favour the experimental realisations that made the many-body physics visible and controllable, but the omission of Jaksch and the Zoller/Cirac contribution would be awkward.
assessment.maturity: Mature and robust across many groups; the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely, although quantum simulation's practical payoff is still developing.
uncertainties: Theory versus experiment balance in the allocation is unresolved.
Several other strong contributors (for example Kasevich, Hulet, Ketterle-related precursors) are outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and the topological insulator concept opened a new classification of electronic matter, with lasting influence on condensed-matter physics, spintronics and topological quantum devices. Originality and clarity are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells (with Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang proposing the HgTe route, who are not credited). Hasan is a key ARPES contributor to 3D topological insulators, so credit for the 3D branch would be left out of this trio.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent confirmations and a stable theoretical framework; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) is not in the supplied names.
Division between 2D and 3D topological insulators may need different recognition.
Outside my core area; I defer partly to condensed-matter colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks with magic-wavelength trapping achieved fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, redefining precision measurement and enabling tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The idea is original and the demonstration clear and decisive.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock; Ye led the work to extreme precision and coherence. A two-person prize is clean, though Hall and Hänsch were already honoured for the frequency comb that underpins the clocks.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with multiple independent clocks around the world agreeing at the 1e-18 level; the redefinition of the second is still pending, which suggests timing is reasonable but not urgent.
uncertainties: The pending redefinition of the SI second may make the committee wish to wait.
The relationship to earlier ion-clock and comb prizes may invite a view that this is an incremental extension.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new field of correlated moire matter: flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity tunable in a single device. It is a striking new regime of physics with enormous follow-on activity.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed the correlated insulator and superconductivity. The trio is a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration, though Cao and Fatemi, who did much of the experiment, are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Relatively young, with strong but still evolving understanding of the superconducting mechanism and sample-dependent reproducibility. Probably slightly premature.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity remains debated.
Sample dependence and reproducibility across laboratories remain a concern.
First authors of the key experiments are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light overcame the quantum noise limit in interferometers and is now routinely used in gravitational-wave detectors. It is a case where fundamental quantum optics became an enabling technology, and I value the clear link between quantum noise theory and instrument performance.
assessment.attribution: Caves supplied the theory of squeezed-state interferometry; Schnabel demonstrated it at GEO600 and developed the technology; Mavalvala contributed to LIGO's implementation. Kimble and others contributed substantial experiments and could be argued for instead, and the collaborative nature of the LIGO implementation clouds credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the sense of deployment in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600 with repeated demonstration; the recognition of gravitational waves in 2017 reduces the urgency.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among the many groups in squeezing is unresolved.
Part of the impact is already recognised via the 2017 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg-blockade tweezer arrays gave programmable, large-scale quantum simulation and gate operations with neutral atoms, including observation of exotic phases and growing fidelities. It is a fast-moving and important platform for quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Lukin, Browaeys and Saffman were each central to blockade physics and arrays, but Jaksch, Zoller and others proposed the Rydberg gate and Bernien, Endres, Lukin, Browaeys and Lahaye contributed key experiments. The best trio is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Somewhat premature: very rapid progress, but long-term robustness of error-corrected operation and comparison with other platforms remain unsettled.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among theorists and experimentalists is unclear.
Competing platforms mean the lasting significance is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of quantum error correction and topological codes showed that fault tolerance is possible in principle, a conceptual breakthrough that underpins the entire quantum computing programme. As a hardware-minded theorist, I would stress that experimental demonstrations below threshold are now emerging, giving the theory empirical weight.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane introduced the first quantum error-correcting codes and Kitaev introduced the surface and toric code and fault tolerance; Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme and others are not in the supplied credit, so the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Theoretically mature, but experimental validation of large-scale error correction is still developing, and it is not yet clear the prize would be for a discovery in physics rather than for information theory.
uncertainties: Fit with the physics prize criteria is uncertain.
Many contributors are outside the supplied credited names.
Fault-tolerant quantum computing is still ahead of us.
